title: Storage limitations and privacy
learningObjectives: Explain storage limitations and privacy and apply safe browser programming practices.

understand.concept: Browser storage is origin-scoped and subject to browser policies, quotas, user clearing, private browsing behaviour, and possible eviction. localStorage and sessionStorage are not secure vaults. IndexedDB is better suited to larger structured client-side data, but it is not a substitute for server authorization.
understand.whyItMatters: Assuming browser storage is permanent or secret can cause data loss and security issues. Store only what is appropriate for the client and revalidate important data on a trusted backend.
understand.analogy: A browser store is a convenient local drawer, not a bank vault or permanent archive.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser APIs, security boundaries, and accessibility requirements are defined by web platform standards.

practise.guidedTask: List which data belongs in browser storage and which must remain server-side. Simulate malformed JSON and unavailable storage.
practise.independentTask: Build a small browser feature using the API or safety principle. Test normal, denied, unavailable, and invalid cases where relevant.
hints: Treat data from the browser, URL, and network as untrusted.
Ask permission only after explaining the purpose.
Keep sensitive authorization and secrets on a trusted backend.

questions.prompt: Should a frontend app store authentication secrets in localStorage?
options: No, it is accessible to same-origin scripts and is not a secure vault
questions.answer: No, it is accessible to same-origin scripts and is not a secure vault
questions.explanation: Web Storage is readable by scripts executing in the origin and should not hold sensitive authentication secrets.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach for browser-facing features?
options: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
Assume every browser grants every permission
questions.answer: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
questions.explanation: Browser features should respect user choice, validate inputs, and enforce protected actions on the server.
